lessons.title: Personal hygiene, water and health

blocks.md: **Hygiene** means the practices that keep us clean and prevent disease. **Personal hygiene**: bathe regularly, wash hands with soap and clean water, brush teeth, keep nails short, wear clean clothes and cover the mouth when coughing or sneezing. Washing hands before eating and cooking, and after using the toilet, prevents many illnesses such as diarrhoea.

blocks.caption: Four steps to wash hands
blocks.alt: Four boxes showing wet, soap and rub, rinse and dry.

blocks.title: Hand washing steps
blocks.md:
1. Wet hands with clean water.
2. Apply soap and rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers and under nails for at least 20 seconds.
3. Rinse with clean water.
4. Dry with a clean cloth or air dry.
If there is no soap, use clean water and ash or another safe method, but soap is better.

blocks.title: Water, food and surroundings
blocks.md: Drink **safe water**: from a protected source, or boiled or treated. Store it in clean, covered containers. Wash fruit and vegetables, cook food well and keep it covered from flies. Use latrines or toilets; never defecate near water sources. Dispose of waste properly and drain stagnant water.

**Malaria** is a disease spread by the bite of infected female *Anopheles* mosquitoes. Symptoms often include fever, chills, headache and weakness. To prevent it: **sleep under a treated mosquito net**, clear stagnant water and bushes around the house, cover water containers, use window screens and protective clothing. Anyone with fever should go quickly to a health centre for a test and treatment; do not rely on guesses.

blocks.title: A balanced diet
blocks.md: A balanced diet contains **energy foods** (cassava, rice, yam, bread), **body-building foods** (beans, fish, eggs, meat, groundnuts), and **protective foods** (fruits and vegetables, which give vitamins and minerals), plus water. Eating many different foods, in good quantity, helps children grow, learn and fight disease.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Clear water is not always safe: it may still carry germs.
- Taking medicine without a test or advice can be dangerous.
- One food group alone does not make a balanced diet.

blocks.title: Example 1: malaria prevention
blocks.statement: Give two ways a family can protect itself from malaria.
steps: Sleep under a treated mosquito net.
Remove standing water where mosquitoes breed.
blocks.answer: Use treated nets and remove stagnant water.

blocks.title: Example 2: a balanced meal
blocks.statement: Is a meal of only cassava a balanced diet? Explain.
steps: A balanced meal also needs protein and fruits or vegetables.
So it is not balanced; add beans or fish and vegetables.
blocks.answer: No; it needs body-building and protective foods too.
